root_cause: FastAPI 0.123.6 changed Dependant.is_gen_callable / is_async_gen_callable / is_coroutine_callable to fall back to inspecting getattr(call, '__call__'). When the dependency is a class (Depends() on a class annotation) whose instances define an async/generator __call__, the class's __call__ attribute is that unbound function, so the class itself was misclassified as a coroutine/generator. FastAPI then awaited or iterated the class constructor result instead of just instantiating it.
best_solution: In each of the three is_*_callable cached properties in fastapi/dependencies/models.py, after the direct function checks on self.call and before the dunder_call fallback, add `if inspect.isclass(_unwrapped_call(self.call)): return False`. A class is called to build an instance; calling it is synchronous and never yields, whatever its instances' __call__ looks like. Also drop the stale comment that said the class case was covered by the default return. The statement names the three methods and the check, so the fix follows directly from it.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_dependency_class.py::test_class_dependency gets four new parametrized routes: /callable-dependency-class, /callable-gen-dependency-class, /async-callable-dependency-class and /async-callable-gen-dependency-class. Each uses `instance: <Class> = Depends()` with CallableDependency, CallableGenDependency, AsyncCallableDependency or AsyncCallableGenDependency, and the handler calls the instance itself. The injected value must be an instance of the class, not an awaited or iterated __call__ result. No new API or exact string is required.
locating_signals: The statement names the exact functions (is_coroutine_callable, is_async_gen_callable, is_gen_callable), the concept dunder_call, and the fix (check whether the callable is a class before inspecting dunder_call). Grepping for dunder_call or is_gen_callable leads straight to fastapi/dependencies/models.py.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs (v4, v6, v7, v8) passed in the Kaggle env, in 68-90s with 17-23 calls. v8 is the closest to gold: isclass(_impartial(self.call)) at the same three points. v4 also adds a redundant second isclass check on _unwrapped_call before dunder_unwrapped_call. That is harmless. v6 uses isclass(self.call) with no unwrapping, which would miss a functools.partial of a class, and it leaves a stray test file behind. v7 puts the check after the `dunder_call is None` guard and leaves a reproduce_issue.py script in the repo. Both still pass the hidden tests.
generalizable_lesson: When a type-detection helper falls back to inspecting obj.__call__, guard against classes first with inspect.isclass: a class's __call__ attribute is its instances' method, not how the class itself behaves when called. More generally, when the statement is a PR description naming the functions and the check to add, apply that exact check at the same point in every function it lists, unwrap the object the same way the nearby code does (partial or wrapped), and delete scratch reproduce and test files before finishing.
acceptable_alternatives: Using isclass on self.call, _impartial(self.call) or _unwrapped_call(self.call) all pass. Putting the check after the dunder_call None-guard (v7) also passes. The only requirement is that it runs before the dunder_call coroutine/generator inspection in all three methods.
